questions.label: NGS-01
questions.title: Angular Signal Definition
questions.prompt: What does `computed()` provide in Angular Signals?
questions.explanation: `computed` derives values from other signals and is read-only.

questions.label: NGS-02
questions.title: Angular Signal Definition
questions.prompt: Which API updates signal state inside @ngrx/signals SignalStore?
questions.explanation: SignalStore uses `patchState(store, partial)` for immutable partial updates.

questions.label: NGS-03
questions.title: Angular Signal Definition
questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of `effect()` with signals?

choices.text: Perform side effects when dependencies change

questions.explanation: `effect` reacts to signal changes and is intended for side effects.

questions.label: NGS-04
questions.title: Angular Signal Definition
questions.prompt: How should a signal value be read in a template?
questions.explanation: Signals are functions. Reading them requires invoking as `signal()`.

questions.label: NGS-05
questions.title: Angular Signal Definition
questions.prompt: What is a key advantage of Signals in Angular change detection?
questions.explanation: Signals update only consumers depending on changed signal values.

questions.label: CD-01
questions.title: Default Change Detection Trigger

choices.text: Many async completions such as timers, promises, XHR, and DOM events patched by Zone.js

questions.explanation: With Zone.js and the Default strategy, Angular is notified after many asynchronous browser operations and can check the component tree.
questions.prompt: In a Zone.js-based Angular app using `ChangeDetectionStrategy.Default`, what usually causes Angular to run change detection?

questions.label: CD-02
questions.title: OnPush and Plain Properties

choices.text: It updates immediately on every interval tick
It updates only if the property is public
It usually stays stale because the component was not marked for check
Angular throws because OnPush forbids timers

questions.explanation: OnPush checks a component when it is marked by specific triggers. A plain timer mutation is not enough by itself.
questions.prompt: A component uses `ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush`. A `setInterval()` mutates a plain class property, but no input changes, event, async pipe emission, signal update, or manual mark occurs. What happens to the template?

questions.label: CD-03
questions.title: Valid OnPush Triggers

choices.text: A new input value or object reference from the parent
Mutating an arbitrary nested object property without changing a reference

questions.explanation: OnPush reacts to explicit framework notifications such as input reference changes, template events, async pipe emissions, signal updates, and manual change detector calls.
questions.prompt: Which events can mark an OnPush component for checking?

questions.label: CD-04
questions.title: Signals with OnPush

choices.text: Signals force Angular to check every component on every browser task
Signal reads are tracked, and signal updates can mark dependent views for efficient updates
Signals are just aliases for RxJS `BehaviorSubject`

questions.explanation: Signals make dependencies explicit. When a signal read by a template changes, Angular can update the dependent view without relying on broad async patching.
questions.prompt: Why do signals fit well with OnPush change detection?

questions.label: CD-05
questions.title: Zoneless Plain Variables

choices.text: Without Zone.js, the timer completion itself is not an automatic change detection notification
Plain class properties are compile-time constants
The template must use `| async` for every value

questions.explanation: Zoneless mode relies on explicit notifications such as signals, events, async pipe emissions, input changes, or manual marking.
questions.prompt: In a zoneless Angular app, why does updating a plain class property inside `setInterval()` often not update the template?

questions.label: RXS-01
questions.title: BehaviorSubject as State

choices.text: It stores a current value and emits values to subscribers
It can only emit once and then completes

questions.explanation: `BehaviorSubject` has a current value and an observable stream, which makes it useful for small local state examples.
questions.prompt: Why is `BehaviorSubject<T>` useful as a simple local state holder?

questions.label: RXS-02
questions.title: Derived Observable State

choices.text: Read only `options$.value` once in the constructor

questions.explanation: `combineLatest` derives a stream from multiple source streams and recalculates when either source emits.
questions.prompt: When `selectedValue$` depends on both `options$` and `selectedKey$`, which RxJS pattern fits best?

questions.label: RXS-03
questions.title: debounceTime(0)

choices.text: To wait a full second before every emission
To collapse synchronous updates so derived logic sees the final state
To convert an Observable into a signal

questions.explanation: `debounceTime(0)` yields to the event loop, allowing multiple synchronous `.next()` calls to settle before mapping.
questions.prompt: In the course example, why is `debounceTime(0)` used after `combineLatest()`?

questions.label: RXS-04
questions.title: Avoiding Stale Derived Reads

choices.text: It makes the read, guard, and write happen against one source of truth
It prevents TypeScript from checking the object
It removes the need for immutable updates

questions.explanation: Keeping related state together helps avoid stale decisions caused by async gaps between reading derived state and writing source state.
questions.prompt: Why does the lesson recommend storing related values like `a` and `b` in one state object when an update depends on their sum?

questions.label: SIG-01
questions.title: Reading a Signal
questions.explanation: Angular signals are callable value containers. Calling the signal reads its current value.
questions.prompt: How do you read the current value of `const count = signal(0)`?

questions.label: SIG-02
questions.title: set() vs update()

choices.text: `set()` replaces the value; `update()` derives the next value from the previous value
`set()` only works in templates; `update()` only works in constructors
`set()` creates a computed signal; `update()` creates an effect
Both methods are only available on `computed()` signals

questions.explanation: `set(value)` writes a specific value, while `update(fn)` receives the previous value and returns the next value.
questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes `set()` and `update()` on a writable signal?

questions.label: SIG-03
questions.title: Computed Signals

choices.text: A writable signal that must be manually updated
A derived read-only signal that recalculates from its signal dependencies

questions.explanation: `computed()` creates a read-only derived signal from the signals read inside its function.
questions.prompt: What does `computed(() => count() * 2)` provide?

questions.label: SIG-04
questions.title: Calling Signals in Templates

choices.text: Signals are tracked reactive reads, so Angular can know which bindings depend on them
Signals are executed only once at build time
Angular converts every method call into a signal automatically

questions.explanation: Signal calls are part of Angular's reactive model, so the framework can track dependencies precisely.
questions.prompt: Why is `{{ count() }}` acceptable in an Angular template even though arbitrary method calls in templates are often discouraged?

questions.label: CTX-01
questions.title: Where inject() Works

choices.text: A component or service field initializer
An arbitrary click handler called later by the user

questions.explanation: `inject()` requires an injection context. Field initializers, constructors, factories, and functions run with `runInInjectionContext()` are valid contexts.
questions.prompt: Where can `inject()` normally be called without passing an explicit injector?

questions.label: CTX-02
questions.title: DestroyRef Cleanup

choices.text: Registering cleanup so the subscription is unsubscribed when the component is destroyed
Converting an Observable into a signal
Forcing a required input to become optional

questions.explanation: `DestroyRef.onDestroy()` registers teardown logic tied to the lifecycle of the injection context.
questions.prompt: What is `DestroyRef` used for in the interval subscription example?

questions.label: CTX-03
questions.title: Creating Effects Later

choices.text: Pass `{ injector: this.injector }` to `effect()` or run the code in an injection context

questions.explanation: Effects need an injection context so Angular can tie their lifetime to cleanup services such as `DestroyRef`.
questions.prompt: A method wants to create an `effect()` after construction. What is the correct pattern shown in the course?

questions.label: CTX-04
questions.title: Stopping an Effect

choices.text: Set the effect variable to `undefined` only

questions.explanation: `effect()` returns an `EffectRef`. Calling `destroy()` stops that effect.
questions.prompt: How can a manually stored `EffectRef` be stopped before the component is destroyed?

questions.label: CME-01
questions.title: Good computed() Usage

choices.text: Reading one or more writable signals
Creating a new signal every time the computed runs
Returning a value derived from immutable non-signal constants

questions.explanation: A computed should derive a value from signals and stable data. It should not create signals or perform side effects.
questions.prompt: Which are good uses inside a `computed()` function?

questions.label: CME-02
questions.title: Bad computed() Usage
questions.explanation: Computed functions should be pure derivations. Writing to a signal inside a computed is a side effect and can create invalid reactive flows.
questions.prompt: Which implementation is a poor fit for `computed()`?

questions.label: CME-03
questions.title: Effect Purpose

choices.text: Performing a side effect such as logging or saving when signals change

questions.explanation: Effects rerun when the signals they read change and are intended for side effects, not primary state derivation.
questions.prompt: What is an appropriate use for `effect()`?

questions.label: CME-04
questions.title: Effect Re-execution

choices.text: The effect can run once with the latest accumulated values
The effect must run once per changed signal synchronously

questions.explanation: Effects are scheduled reactive work and can observe the latest values after multiple changes are accumulated.
questions.prompt: If multiple signal dependencies change before Angular flushes an effect, what does the course emphasize?

questions.label: INT-01
questions.title: Signal to Observable

choices.text: Converts a signal into an RxJS Observable that emits when the signal changes
Converts an Observable into a writable signal

questions.explanation: `toObservable()` exposes signal state to RxJS pipelines.
questions.prompt: What does `toObservable(this.number)` do?

questions.label: INT-02
questions.title: Observable to Signal

choices.text: Signals always need a current value, while an async Observable may not emit immediately
It makes the Observable emit synchronously
It turns the returned signal into an output

questions.explanation: Without an initial value, the signal value may be `undefined` until the first Observable emission.
questions.prompt: Why is `initialValue` commonly passed to `toSignal()` for asynchronous Observables?

questions.label: INT-03
questions.title: requireSync

choices.text: Only when `source$` is guaranteed to emit synchronously during subscription

questions.explanation: `requireSync: true` asserts that the Observable emits immediately. Angular throws if that is not true.
questions.prompt: When should `toSignal(source$, { requireSync: true })` be used?

questions.label: INT-04
questions.title: Interop Creation Context

choices.text: `ngOnInit()` is not itself an injection context
RxJS interop APIs only work in services
Signals cannot be created after construction

questions.explanation: By default these APIs use the current injection context for cleanup. Outside such a context, pass an `Injector` option.
questions.prompt: Why can calling `toSignal()` or `toObservable()` in `ngOnInit()` fail unless an injector is provided?

questions.label: INT-05
questions.title: Immutable Array Updates
questions.explanation: Array and object signal values should be replaced with new references rather than mutated in place.
questions.prompt: Which update is preferred for adding `Dana` to `names = signal(['Alice'])`?

questions.label: API-01
questions.title: Functional Guard Syntax
questions.explanation: Functional guards use function types such as `CanActivateFn` and can call `inject()` inside the guard function.
questions.prompt: Which modern guard style replaces many class-based `CanActivate` guard classes?

questions.label: API-02
questions.title: Old and New Input APIs

choices.text: Old: `@Input() title!: string`; New: `readonly title = input.required<string>()`

questions.explanation: Decorator inputs remain supported, while new code can use signal input initializer functions.
questions.prompt: Which pair correctly matches old and new Angular input declaration styles?

questions.label: API-03
questions.title: Deriving from Signal Inputs

choices.text: Because `input()` values are signals and `computed()` reruns when the input signals it reads change
Because required inputs never change after initialization
Because pipes automatically create computed signals
Because `ngOnChanges()` is required only for services

questions.explanation: Signal inputs are read with `amount()` or `currency()`, so computed values can derive from them reactively.
questions.prompt: In the currency converter example, why can `converted` be a `computed()` signal instead of recalculated in `ngOnChanges()`?

questions.label: API-04
questions.title: Old and New Output APIs
questions.explanation: `output()` declares a component output and returns an emitter ref with `.emit()`.
questions.prompt: Which new output API is the counterpart to `@Output() refreshRequired = new EventEmitter<void>()`?

questions.label: API-05
questions.title: Outputs Are Events

choices.text: It represents events and emits with `.emit()`
It automatically bubbles like a native DOM event

questions.explanation: Outputs are event emitters, not state signals. Custom Angular outputs do not bubble through the DOM.
questions.prompt: Which statement about `output()` is correct?

questions.label: API-06
questions.title: model() and Two-way Binding

choices.text: A writable signal that also participates in input/output two-way binding

questions.explanation: `model()` creates a writable model input and pairs naturally with `[(selected)]`.
questions.prompt: What does `model.required<string>()` provide in the option selector example?

questions.label: API-07
questions.title: Binding a Model to a Signal
questions.explanation: For model binding to a writable signal, pass the signal instance, not the current signal value.
questions.prompt: When a parent has `currency = signal('USD')`, what is the correct banana-in-a-box binding to a child model named `selected`?

questions.label: API-08
questions.title: Signal View Queries

choices.text: A signal whose value is the queried component instance or `undefined` until available
A plain property automatically assigned before the constructor

questions.explanation: Signal queries expose query results as signals. Optional queries can be `undefined` until Angular creates the result.
questions.prompt: What does `viewChild(CurrencyConverterComponent)` return in the new query API?

questions.label: API-09
questions.title: Required Query Timing

choices.text: It removes `undefined` from the type, but reading too early can still throw because the view is not created yet
It can only query projected content
It must be used with `@ViewChild()` at the same time

questions.explanation: Required query results are not available earlier just because the type is required.
questions.prompt: What is a key caution for `viewChild.required(...)`?

questions.label: API-10
questions.title: Projected Template Query

choices.text: To capture a projected `TemplateRef` as a signal and render it where the component chooses
To mutate raw DOM nodes outside Angular rendering
To replace all inputs with outputs
To force the parent to use Zone.js

questions.explanation: A marker directive can inject `TemplateRef`, and `contentChild()` lets the component reactively access the projected template.
questions.prompt: In the custom option template example, why use a directive plus `contentChild()`?

questions.label: API-11
questions.title: Signal-driven Host Bindings

choices.text: Use directive `host` metadata such as `'[style.color]': 'color()'` and `'(click)': 'invert()'`
Copy the signal into a plain property with an effect just for `@HostBinding()`
Use direct DOM manipulation in every click handler

questions.explanation: Host metadata keeps signal-driven host bindings declarative and avoids a needless signal-to-property bridge.
questions.prompt: Which directive pattern is preferred in the RGB example for binding host color and click behavior?

questions.label: API-12
questions.title: outputFromObservable

choices.text: When the event source is already an RxJS stream and should be exposed as an Angular output
When the child needs writable state from the parent
When an input should become required
When a `computed()` value needs to become mutable

questions.explanation: `outputFromObservable()` subscribes to an Observable and forwards its `next` values as output events until the component is destroyed.
questions.prompt: When is `outputFromObservable(refreshRequired$)` a good fit?

questions.label: RTR-01
questions.title: Router Feature Functions
questions.explanation: The sample configures hash URLs and binds route data/params directly to component inputs.
questions.prompt: Which router feature functions are used in the lesson's `provideRouter()` setup?

questions.label: RTR-02
questions.title: Route Param Changes

choices.text: Angular may reuse the same component instance when only the route parameter changes
Signals cannot be used with the router

questions.explanation: Navigating from one detail id to another can keep the same component instance alive, so the component must respond to new params.
questions.prompt: Why must a movie details component react to route parameter changes instead of only reading the initial route value?

questions.label: RTR-03
questions.title: Signal Route Input
questions.explanation: Route params are strings by default, so `numberAttribute` converts the bound value for numeric comparisons.
questions.prompt: With `withComponentInputBinding()` enabled and a route parameter named `id`, which component field can receive it as a signal input?

questions.label: RTR-04
questions.title: switchMap for Route-driven Requests

choices.text: It cancels or unsubscribes from the previous request stream when a new parameter arrives
It converts all route params to numbers automatically
It makes `ActivatedRoute` unnecessary in every case

questions.explanation: `switchMap()` keeps the latest route-driven async work active and drops older in-flight work.
questions.prompt: Why is `switchMap()` useful when route params trigger HTTP requests?

questions.label: RTR-05
questions.title: Observable vs Signal in Templates

choices.text: Observable and Signal: always use `await` in the template

questions.explanation: Observables are unwrapped with `AsyncPipe`; signals are read by calling them.
questions.prompt: Which template usage correctly matches the component state shape?

questions.label: FRM-01
questions.title: Signal Forms Model

choices.text: It stores the form data model as signal state

questions.explanation: The signal form is built around a signal-backed model object.
questions.prompt: In the subscribe form sample, what is `subscribeModel = signal<Subscription>(initialData)` used for?

questions.label: FRM-02
questions.title: Creating a Signal Form
questions.explanation: The example imports `form` from `@angular/forms/signals` and passes the model signal plus schema.
questions.prompt: Which expression creates the signal form in the course example?

questions.label: FRM-03
questions.title: Binding Inputs to Fields
questions.explanation: The sample uses the `FormField` directive and binds each control with `[formField]`.
questions.prompt: How does the template bind an input element to the email field in the signal form?

questions.label: FRM-04
questions.title: Conditional Validators

choices.text: The `required(rootPath.email, { when: ({ valueOf }) => valueOf(rootPath.sendViaEmail) === true })` rule
The placeholder text on the input

questions.explanation: The `when` predicate uses reactive form state to apply the required rule only when email delivery is selected.
questions.prompt: What makes the email field conditionally required in `SubscriptionSchema`?

questions.label: FRM-05
questions.title: Reading Field State
questions.explanation: Signal forms expose reactive state through callable form and field accessors such as `valid()`, `invalid()`, and `errors()`.
questions.prompt: Which field/form state methods are shown in the signal form comments or template?

questions.label: SVC-01
questions.title: Private Writable, Public Read-only

choices.text: To let consumers read questions without allowing them to mutate the service's writable signal directly
To prevent templates from reading questions

questions.explanation: A common service pattern is private writable state plus public read-only signal access.
questions.prompt: Why does `ExamService` keep `#questions = signal<Question[]>(...)` private and expose `questions = this.#questions.asReadonly()`?

questions.label: SVC-02
questions.title: Computed Answers

choices.text: An array that maps each selected answer index to whether it matches the corresponding question's `correctAnswerIndex`
A new HTTP request for every question
A router URL for the current question

questions.explanation: `userAnswers` reads private answer state and question state, then derives correctness for each answered question.
questions.prompt: What does the service's `userAnswers` computed signal derive?

questions.label: SVC-03
questions.title: Current Question Index

choices.text: The next unanswered question is at the index equal to the number of answers already submitted

questions.explanation: If answers are stored in order, the count of submitted answers points to the next question index.
questions.prompt: In `ExamService`, why can `currentQuestionIndex` be computed from `this.userAnswers().length`?

questions.label: SVC-04
questions.title: Quiz Done Signal
questions.explanation: `isQuizDone` is derived state, so `computed()` is the appropriate signal API.
questions.prompt: Which expression best describes `isQuizDone` in the service?
